title: The Fibonacci Rectangle Game: Two First-Move Classes and a Triangle-Induced Choice
summary: A square-adjoining rectangle game generates the Fibonacci numbers and the Fibonacci spiral from a simple geometric rule. If one starts from a square, the four possible first moves are all equivalent by rotation. If one starts instead from a non-square rectangle, there are still four geometric placements for the first square, but they split into exactly two equivalence classes: long-side-first and short-side-first.
